newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon MEA lost $50 mln in 1996 - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon MEA lost $50 mln in 1996 - chairman.

text.p: Lebanon's Middle East Airlines made a $50 million loss in 1996 and is expected to lose $20 million in 1997, MEA Chairman Khaled Salam said on Thursday.
Salam said he did not foresee a net profit before 1999.
"The company lost $50 million in 1996, and is expected to lose $20 million in 1997 before breaking even in 1998," he told Reuters.
Salam said Israel's 17-day blitz on Lebanon in April which cost MEA about $12 million in lost revenue, coupled with the rise in international fuel prices caused the 1996 losses.
Salam told Reuters previously that he expected the company's revenues to rise 10 percent in 1997 from about $300 million in 1996.
MEA is 99-percent owned by the Bank of Lebanon under a $100 million debt-for-equity swap last September that wiped the airline's debts accumulated between 1990 and 1995.
The central bank contributed another $31 million in November and will add $94 million by mid-1998 to complete the $225 million planned capital increase.
